steps.name: spaces required per unit before the reform (baseline-weighted)
steps.formula: spaces required per unit, baseline-weighted over counties and 2-, 3-4- and 5+-unit buildings = 1.55 spaces/unit

steps.name: spaces still built per unit after the reform (baseline-weighted)
steps.formula: spaces still built per unit = required x share still built (transit-rich 0.6, elsewhere 0.925), weighted by the transit-rich share of each county's homes = 1.11 spaces/unit

steps.name: spaces avoided per unit
steps.formula: spaces required per unit before the reform (baseline-weighted) (1.55 spaces/unit) − spaces still built per unit after the reform (baseline-weighted) (1.11 spaces/unit) = 0.442 spaces/unit

inputs.name: spaces required per unit before the reform (baseline-weighted)

steps.name: cost per space avoided (baseline-weighted mix)
steps.formula: cost per space avoided = average saving / average spaces avoided, from the surface, structured and underground mix of each tract class

steps.name: baseline units 2027-2031, building types reached

steps.name: value per new unit (effective)

steps.name: saving as a share of value
steps.formula: fee saving per unit ($25,000/unit) ÷ value per new unit (effective) ($259,449/unit) = 0.0964

sentence.text: Over 2027–2031, Pennsylvania would likely permit between 12,000 and 30,000 more homes (9.7–26%) with accessory dwelling units (ADUs) allowed, two to six homes allowed on single-family lots, more homes allowed near major transit stops, parking minimums removed and development fees cut in half, on top of a baseline of 67,000–180,000 homes expected under today's rules.

cites.value: baseline permitted units 2027-2031, state

label.text: Baseline: homes permitted under today's rules

why.text: Middle estimate: 6.2% more homes than the baseline. “Adds a lot” means at least 5%.
Middle estimate: 0.35% more homes than the baseline. “Little effect” means under 1%.
Middle estimate: 0.22% more homes than the baseline. “Little effect” means under 1%.
Middle estimate: 2.1% more homes than the baseline. “Adds some” means 1% to under 5%.
Middle estimate: 4.9% more homes than the baseline. “Adds some” means 1% to under 5%.

meaning.text: Lots the rule reaches: existing homes of the building types in scope, counted as lots.

steps.formula: P10, P50, P90 of 2,000 seeded draws of the sum over tracts of eligible lots = sum over building types in scope of [census homes of that type / homes per building] x lot-count correction x (1 - already-legal share) x share of the tract inside the scenario's places = 3,185,017 lots, 3,336,025 lots, 3,496,588 lots

label.text: Lots with room for an ADU

meaning.text: Of those, lots with enough yard for a backyard home of the required size.

steps.formula: P10, P50, P90 of 2,000 seeded draws of the sum over tracts of lots with room = sum over building types of eligible lots x fit share f(type, area type) = 1,587,259 lots, 1,884,686 lots, 2,158,937 lots

label.text: Lots where an ADU is feasible

meaning.text: Of those, lots where rent would pay for building one, or where the owner would build one for family anyway.

steps.formula: P10, P50, P90 of 2,000 seeded draws of the sum over tracts of feasible lots = lots with room x p, where p = p_rent + family-use share x (1 - p_rent) and p_rent = share of the tract's cash rents at or above break-even rent / (one-bedroom ratio x new-unit premium) = 112,910 lots, 202,321 lots, 325,656 lots

cites.shown: ADUs built 2027-2031

meaning.text: Of those, the ones expected to be built over the five years, with a slow start while owners learn about the new right.

steps.formula: P10, P50, P90 of 2,000 seeded draws of the sum over tracts of ADUs built = feasible lots x yearly take-up h x sum over 2027-2031 of ramp(t) x ADUs per lot n = 3,984 units, 9,055 units, 17,673 units

cites.value: net added units 2027-2031 (adu: sf_detached, sf_attached)
cites.shown: Net added units 2027-2031

meaning.text: What is left after taking out homes that would have been built anyway: the reform's own addition.

steps.formula: P10, P50, P90 of 2,000 seeded draws of the sum over tracts of net added units = ADUs built x (1 - displacement share x) = 3,481 units, 8,011 units, 15,671 units

label.text: Eligible single-family lots in single-family-only zones

meaning.text: Single-family lots in zones that allow only one home today.

steps.formula: P10, P50, P90 of 2,000 seeded draws of the sum over tracts of eligible lots = max(census single-family homes x lot-count correction x single-family-only zoned share - ADU overlap share x lots used by ADUs, 0) = 1,873,911 lots, 2,180,643 lots, 2,455,296 lots

label.text: Lots large enough for a 2-6 unit building

cites.value: lots large enough for a 2-6 unit building (missing_middle: sf_detached)
cites.shown: Lots large enough for a 2-6 unit building

meaning.text: Of those, lots big enough for a small apartment building or townhouses.

steps.formula: P10, P50, P90 of 2,000 seeded draws of the sum over tracts of lots large enough = eligible lots x f, where f is the measured share, else the share of homes whose block land per home x lot share is at least the smallest lot for a 2-6 unit building, else the ledger fit share = 1,501,556 lots, 1,760,709 lots, 2,010,356 lots

meaning.text: Of those, lots where a new small building would be worth more than the house and the cost of building it.

steps.formula: P10, P50, P90 of 2,000 seeded draws of the sum over tracts of feasible lots = lots large enough x sum over k = 2..6 of mix weight w_k x p_k, where p_k = share of the tract's owner home values at or below residual land value of a k-unit building / (1 + acquisition premium) = 3,582 lots, 14,493 lots, 40,164 lots

meaning.text: Neighbourhoods with frequent transit nearby.

steps.formula: transit-rich tracts = 814 of 3445 (at least half of the tract's homes within 1/2 mile of rail or 1/4 mile of a bus stop with 64+ weekday departures, or a major stop inside the tract)

label.text: Spaces required per unit before the reform

meaning.text: Parking spaces the rules require for each new home today.

steps.formula: spaces required per unit, baseline-weighted over counties and 2-, 3-4- and 5+-unit buildings = 1.55 spaces/unit

label.text: Spaces still built per unit after the reform

meaning.text: Parking spaces builders would still choose to build without a rule.

steps.formula: spaces still built per unit = required x share still built (transit-rich 0.6, elsewhere 0.925), weighted by the transit-rich share of each county's homes = 1.11 spaces/unit

meaning.text: Spaces no longer built for each new home.

steps.formula: spaces required per unit before the reform (baseline-weighted) (1.55 spaces/unit) − spaces still built per unit after the reform (baseline-weighted) (1.11 spaces/unit) = 0.442 spaces/unit

meaning.text: What each space not built would have cost.

steps.formula: cost per space avoided = average saving / average spaces avoided, from the surface, structured and underground mix of each tract class

meaning.text: The saving on each new home from building fewer spaces.

steps.formula: spaces avoided per unit (0.442 spaces/unit) × cost per space avoided (baseline-weighted mix) ($27,440/space) = $12,120/unit

cites.shown: Baseline units 2027-2031, building types reached

meaning.text: Homes the baseline expects to be permitted in the building types this reform reaches.

steps.formula: baseline units 2027-2031 in the building types this reform reaches = 63,412 units (projected from building permits)

meaning.text: What a typical new home is worth, so the saving can be compared with it.

steps.formula: value per new unit, effective = average saving / baseline-weighted average of (saving / value) over counties and building types = $220,187/unit (county medians from ACS brackets x (1 + new-construction premium); rented types capitalised at the cap rate)

label.text: Saving as a share of value

meaning.text: The saving as a share of a new home's value: the size of the push to build.

steps.formula: parking saving per unit ($12,120/unit) ÷ value per new unit (effective) ($220,187/unit) = 0.055

label.text: Medium-run supply response to a change in profit per unit

meaning.text: How strongly builders respond when building becomes more profitable.

steps.formula: Medium-run supply response to a change in profit per unit = 1 (ledger supply.elasticity_medium_run, central)

label.text: Share of a cost saving that reaches the decision to build

meaning.text: How much of the saving reaches the decision to build, rather than land prices.

steps.formula: Share of a cost saving that reaches the decision to build = 0.5 (ledger supply.saving_passthrough_k, central)

label.text: Added units from the parking cost saving, central values

meaning.text: Extra homes because each home costs less to build, at central values.

steps.formula: baseline units 2027-2031, building types reached (63,412 units) × Medium-run supply response to a change in profit per unit (1) × saving as a share of value (0.055) × Share of a cost saving that reaches the decision to build (0.5) = 1,745 units

label.text: Added units from site yield, central values

meaning.text: Extra homes because land once kept for parking can hold homes, at central values.

steps.formula: baseline units x site-yield gain (0.05) x share of spaces avoided, summed = 902.5 units

label.text: Added units from parking reform, central values

meaning.text: Both parking effects together, at central values.

steps.formula: added units from the parking cost saving, central values (1,745 units) + added units from site yield, central values (902.5 units) = 2,648 units

meaning.text: The same chain worked out in every simulated draw, with every uncertain input varied together.

steps.formula: P10, P50, P90 of 2,000 seeded draws of the sum over counties of added units per county in each draw; per draw: baseline units x e x (spaces avoided x cost per space / value per new unit) x k + baseline units x site-yield gain x share of spaces avoided, summed over counties and structure types in each draw = 1,242 units, 2,651 units, 5,088 units

meaning.text: How much the fee cut saves a builder on each new home.

steps.formula: Development fees per unit, all major categories ($50,000/unit) × Cut applied to every fee category (0.5) = $25,000/unit

general.title: What these estimates cannot tell you

items.text: These are likely ranges of building permits, not a forecast of homes finished.
They describe the whole state. They do not say which lots, streets or owners would build.
They do not say who would live in the new homes or what they would pay.
They assume every town follows the new rule from the first day and approves permits at today's pace.
They say nothing about years after the five-year period.
The baseline repeats recent permit trends under today's rules. It does not predict a recession or a boom.
Counties without a permit office, or with imputed permit counts, carry the Census Bureau's estimates.
A lot is counted once. When two reforms could use the same lot, the overlap is taken out.
Savings from one reform that feed another are added; the small cross effect between the fee cut and parking reform is left out.
Whether an ADU fits on a given lot: the fit test is a share for each census tract, not a site plan.
Septic limits, steep slopes, flood zones, historic districts and private deed rules, none of which are in the fit test.
Whether towns slow approvals or add new hurdles.
How quickly owners take up the new right. This is the widest assumption and is not yet checked against places like this state.
For-sale townhouses and condominiums: every new building is valued as a rental.
Which lots sit side by side, or which owners would sell.
The real price of a house bought to be torn down; census home values are owners' own estimates.
Local zoning detail: the share of lots zoned for one home only is a statewide range.
Lending and building-code rules for the larger buildings in this range.
Whether transit service near the stops will keep its current frequency.
Which station areas have land that could be rebuilt.
Whether lenders in a given market would finance buildings with fewer spaces.
Effects on street parking and on neighbours.
Whether land freed from parking becomes homes or something else.
Savings on townhouses, which the permit data count together with detached homes.
Whether towns would replace lost fee revenue with other charges.
Whether roads, pipes or schools paid for by fees would be delayed, which could slow building.
How the saving is shared between landowners, builders and buyers in any one place.

title.text: How many more homes would Pennsylvania permit?

cites.value: baseline permitted units 2027-2031, state

label.text: More homes permitted with the reforms
Baseline: homes permitted under today's rules

body.text: Over 2027–2031, Pennsylvania would likely permit between 12,000 and 30,000 more homes (9.7–26%) with accessory dwelling units (ADUs) allowed, two to six homes allowed on single-family lots, more homes allowed near major transit stops, parking minimums removed and development fees cut in half, on top of a baseline of 67,000–180,000 homes expected under today's rules.

title.text: Accessory dwelling units: Adds a lot

cites.value: baseline permitted units 2027-2031, state

label.text: More homes permitted, this reform alone

meaning.text: Lots the rule reaches: existing homes of the building types in scope, counted as lots.

items.formula: P10, P50, P90 of 2,000 seeded draws of the sum over tracts of eligible lots = sum over building types in scope of [census homes of that type / homes per building] x lot-count correction x (1 - already-legal share) x share of the tract inside the scenario's places = 3,185,017 lots, 3,336,025 lots, 3,496,588 lots

label.text: Lots with room for an ADU

meaning.text: Of those, lots with enough yard for a backyard home of the required size.

items.formula: P10, P50, P90 of 2,000 seeded draws of the sum over tracts of lots with room = sum over building types of eligible lots x fit share f(type, area type) = 1,587,259 lots, 1,884,686 lots, 2,158,937 lots

label.text: Lots where an ADU is feasible

meaning.text: Of those, lots where rent would pay for building one, or where the owner would build one for family anyway.

items.formula: P10, P50, P90 of 2,000 seeded draws of the sum over tracts of feasible lots = lots with room x p, where p = p_rent + family-use share x (1 - p_rent) and p_rent = share of the tract's cash rents at or above break-even rent / (one-bedroom ratio x new-unit premium) = 112,910 lots, 202,321 lots, 325,656 lots

cites.value: ADUs built 2027-2031 (adu: sf_detached, sf_attached)
cites.shown: ADUs built 2027-2031

meaning.text: Of those, the ones expected to be built over the five years, with a slow start while owners learn about the new right.

items.formula: P10, P50, P90 of 2,000 seeded draws of the sum over tracts of ADUs built = feasible lots x yearly take-up h x sum over 2027-2031 of ramp(t) x ADUs per lot n = 3,984 units, 9,055 units, 17,673 units

cites.value: net added units 2027-2031 (adu: sf_detached, sf_attached)
cites.shown: Net added units 2027-2031

meaning.text: What is left after taking out homes that would have been built anyway: the reform's own addition.

items.formula: P10, P50, P90 of 2,000 seeded draws of the sum over tracts of net added units = ADUs built x (1 - displacement share x) = 3,481 units, 8,011 units, 15,671 units

body.text: Middle estimate: 6.2% more homes than the baseline. “Adds a lot” means at least 5%.

title.text: What these estimates cannot tell you

cites.value: baseline permitted units 2027-2031, state

label.text: More homes permitted with the reforms

body.text: These are likely ranges of building permits, not a forecast of homes finished.
They describe the whole state. They do not say which lots, streets or owners would build.
They do not say who would live in the new homes or what they would pay.
They assume every town follows the new rule from the first day and approves permits at today's pace.
They say nothing about years after the five-year period.
Decision support, not a forecast. Not an official state document.
